evals.prompt: ok so i just got claude code installed by our IT guy and i have no idea what im doing. yesterday i asked it to write up notes from a meeting and it says it saved a file but i cannot find it anywhere. all my stuff is normally in downloads. i mostly want help with the monthly board report and sometimes drafting emails to vendors
evals.expected_output: Enters Setup Guide Mode and calibrates to a newcomer. Runs toolcheck.py (or the no-Python one-liner) without asking. Asks intake question 3 (whose machine, may software be installed) before offering installs. Offers missing essential tools as one list of names with a plain why each, no commands; recommends pandoc because the work is documents; installs only after a yes, through a no-admin route, and asks for a new session before writing the toolbox block. Then proposes the workspace in one line (user folder by default), with 'monthly board report' and 'vendor emails' as projects, shows tree and house rules, waits for yes, scaffolds, opens the folder on screen, fills PROGRESS.md, and closes with the habit. Offers to locate yesterday's meeting-notes file and list it as a candidate move rather than moving it.

evals.prompt: can you set up some kind of workspace so you remember things between sessions? i'm on a work laptop (locked down, can't install stuff) and i use you for planning my kitchen remodel and keeping track of my mom's medical appointments. the medical stuff is private.
evals.expected_output: Runs the tool check to see what already exists. Because installing is not allowed, does not install anything or try to work around policy; hands over an IT request list of the missing essential tools with one why each, and writes the toolbox block so Claude knows what is present. Does not offer Tier 2 or edit settings.json, saying why in one sentence. Creates a private/ folder with a one-line README in the medical project and adds the no-summarising rule; keeps the workspace out of a cloud-synced Documents folder. Uses 'kitchen-remodel' and the person's own phrase for the medical project. Shows tree and rules, waits for yes, creates, ends with the habit.

evals.prompt: we set up that claude workspace a couple weeks ago and it's been great. i've got a new thing now, i'm coaching my kid's soccer team and need help with schedules and parent emails. can you add that? also there are like 6 schedule PDFs sitting in my downloads from the league
evals.expected_output: Recognises a repeat visit from ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md or the README and skips the full intake and the toolchain step (re-running toolcheck.py only to confirm). Adds one project folder from the templates and one README bullet without touching existing files. Lists the six PDFs by name with current location, proposed destination, and reason, waits for a yes, moves only those, appends each to inbox/MOVED.md, and says where that list is in plain words.

evals.prompt: new work laptop, windows, not admin. i write python and some terraform for azure, code is in an azure devops repo i cloned to C:\Users\pat\source\repos\infra. set claude up so it's fast and remembers context.
evals.expected_output: Calibrates to a developer: brisk, tool names with versions, commands available. Runs toolcheck.py --roles azure; reports what is present and missing. Uses the no-admin route (Scoop, or winget --scope user and switching a tool to Scoop if an admin prompt appears), installs after a yes, one tool at a time, recommends uv for Python. Asks for a new session, re-runs the check, writes the toolbox block. Offers the read-only permission allow list as a separate yes. Proposes C:\Users\pat\claude_workspace with an 'infra' project whose CONTEXT.md points at the cloned repo; the code stays in the repo and no notes files are added inside it. Skips opening folders on screen.

evals.prompt: my company gave us a shared library of about 150 claude skills and i copied them all into ~/.claude/skills. sessions feel slow to start and claude keeps grabbing the wrong skill. can you clean this up?
evals.expected_output: Counts the installed skills and names the cause in plain words: every installed skill's name and description loads into every session. Checks Tier 2 prerequisites (Python, permission to edit settings.json); if hooks are not allowed, says the vault is not safe there and stops at trimming. Otherwise proposes a pinned / vaulted split with vaulting as the default, proposes a keywords line per vaulted skill in one table, waits for edits and a yes, moves folders to <workspace>/skill_vault/ with a MOVED.md log, installs or confirms the prompt hook, tests three skills surface on typical prompts and an unrelated prompt surfaces nothing, and tells the person to say 'use <skill name>' for a vaulted skill instead of a slash command.
